x: Jack Holden, of Tipton, was now in front and barring accidents looked all over the winner. Never faltering he came round for the final lap and running in splendid style he recorded his first "National" triumph after 10 years of trying.
Bingham trailed Carter, and a few yards behind Bingham came Hoath, who on this lap had moved up to 7th from 13th position. Jack Holden, the oft-times International, was 9th.
Round they came for the second time with Bobby Reid of Birchfield hanging on to Jack Holden's shoulder, and Len Herbert had kept his position and looked a certainty for International honours.

Doubleday was ninth in 1 hour 34 minutes 56 seconds, and White eleventh in 1 hour 36 minutes 0 seconds, the winner being our old Tipton friend, Jack Holden, who covered the course in the very fast time of 1.22.05.

Probably all these successes were helped in no small measure by the great win of Jack Holden in the Marathon on the first day of the meeting, and it must have acted as a great morale-raiser to the rest of the team, so perhaps we can now look forward to Helsinki with a certain degree of confidence.

However, the main part of the season is yet to come and he should find some tough cross-country races a valuable background to his road-running, as have Jack Holden, Jim Peters and Fred Norris before him!
Then to the finish....first man home was Jack Holden of Tipten, a worthy winner. Our first man home was Ted Stimpson in fourth position, scoring 3 for team purposes.
SHOULD THIS TREND CONTINUE IT MAY BE POSSIBLE TO WIN THE 1999 NATIONAL BY FIELDING 97.5 % OF COMPETITORS THUS :- JACK HOLDEN'S GRANDSON.
First home was Jack Holden, of Tipton H., a worthy winner. Our first man home was Ted Stimpson, in fourth position, scoring 3 for team purposes.
Jack Holden reasserted his pre-war dominance despite his mature years on a tough, muddy, ten mile course. A Junior Championship did not yet exist but the Youths' Championship was won easily by G.B.

Despite competing out of season against the in season Australian and New Zealand performers the Home Countries did well with fines wins by John Parlett in the 880 yds, Len Eyre in the 3 miles, Dorothy Tyler in the high jump, Tim Anderson in the pole vault and Jack Holden in the marathon.

Britain's team included the redoubtable veteran Jack Holden, four-times winner of the International Cross Country Champs. and three times "National" champion, and the tough Welshman from South London Harriers, Tom Richards.

Highgate and South London were overtaken by Belgrave’s Jack Flower by the time the race reached Mitcham but Jack was, in turn, passed by the international Jack Holden, who had taken Tipton’s colours to the front.
